title: Static file server with safe paths
when: The user needs a tiny local server for a folder (to test modules or a service worker) or static serving inside a Node backend.
prompt:
Goal: A node:http static server that serves only files inside its root, with correct MIME types, cache headers and a 404.
Steps:
1. Line 1 #!/usr/bin/env node; root = path.resolve(process.argv[2] || "public"); on EADDRINUSE print a hint and set process.exitCode = 1.
2. Decode the pathname in try (400 on a bad escape); file = path.resolve(root, "." + pathname); answer 403 unless it equals root or starts with root + path.sep.
3. Refuse dot files; answer 405 to methods other than GET and HEAD.
4. Folders serve their index.html; missing files serve 404.html when present, else a plain 404.
5. MIME table: html, css, js and mjs as text/javascript, json, svg, png, jpg, webp, woff2, webmanifest; default application/octet-stream.
6. After fs.promises.stat, set content-length and stream with createReadStream(file).pipe(res), answering 500 on stream errors; cache-control: no-cache for HTML.
Quality bar:
- /../secret and %2e%2e cannot leave the root.
- Module scripts load because .js is served as JavaScript.
- Startup prints the URL.
Pitfalls:
- Concatenating the raw URL onto the root.
- readFileSync on every request.
- Serving .env or other dot files.
Verify:
- [ ] A startsWith(root + path.sep) guard on every file.
- [ ] The MIME table covers js and mjs.
- [ ] Statuses 403, 404, 405 exist.
- [ ] Files are streamed.
Output: serve.mjs, run as node serve.mjs [folder] [port].

examples.input: preciso de um servidor local simples para testar meu site
examples.output: serve.mjs serving ./public with a MIME table, traversal guard, index.html for folders, 404 page
